transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I’ve been having trouble going to the toilet — opening my bowels much less often, and I have to strain.
When did you first start having trouble going to the toilet?
It started a while back now, maybe a few weeks.
Do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
No, I don’t have any known allergies to medicines.
How much, if at all, is this affecting your everyday life?
It’s bothering me some — the straining is uncomfortable, and my lower tummy feels bloated.
Are you taking any medicines at the moment, including anything new or recently changed?
I take some tablets for my heart and a calcium one for my bones, and I started some pain tablets not long ago.
Have you ever had an operation or been in hospital?
No, I haven’t had any operations.
Has your appetite, sleep, weight, or energy changed since this started?
I haven’t really noticed any changes in my appetite, sleep, weight, or energy.
Have you noticed anything that seems to make it harder for you to open your bowels?
I think I’ve been drinking less than usual, partly so I don’t have to get up at night.
Is there any health condition you see a doctor or nurse about regularly?
I have arthritis in my back and knees, and I have an irregular heartbeat.
Apart from what you’ve already mentioned, have you noticed any change in how often you pass urine since this started?
I haven’t really noticed any change there.
What worries you most about the trouble you’ve been having opening your bowels?
I’d like something to get things moving, but I’m also worried it could be something serious like bowel cancer.
When you try to go, what does the straining feel like?
It’s uncomfortable — I really have to push, and it feels a bit sore down below.

Are there any other health conditions you take medicines for that we haven’t talked about yet, besides your heart tablets, the calcium tablet for your bones, and the pain tablets you started recently?
No, that’s all — just the arthritis and the irregular heartbeat.

When did you first notice you were going less often and having to strain, did it come on suddenly or build up gradually, and was anything happening around that time that you think might have set it off?
It came on gradually, about three weeks ago. I’d started some pain tablets for my back about a month before that.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed that you’d like to mention?
The stools are hard and pellet-like, but I haven’t seen any blood or black stools, and I haven’t been sick.
How much bother is this trouble going to the toilet causing you at the moment?
It’s quite a bother — the straining is uncomfortable and my lower tummy feels bloated.
Since this started about three weeks ago, has it been happening every day, or does it come and go?
It’s not every day now — I’m going much less often than I used to.
Have you noticed anything else going on with your body that you haven’t mentioned yet?
No, I haven’t noticed anything else.
Are you taking any medicines at the moment — either ones you take regularly or anything new or changed recently?

Yes, I take apixaban 2.5 mg twice a day and bisoprolol 2.5 mg once a day, plus a calcium and vitamin D chewable twice a day. I also started co-codamol 30/500, two tablets four times a day, about a month ago for back pain.
Aside from the medicines you’ve already told me about, do you take anything else for your arthritis, your back or knee pain, or your irregular heartbeat?
No, nothing else — just those ones you mentioned.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
